newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTH AFRICAN BOURSE HEAD CALLS FOR "FRAUD INDEX".
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AFRICAN BOURSE HEAD CALLS FOR "FRAUD INDEX".

text.p: South African business should set up a "fraud index" in order to help fight corporate crime, outgoing Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) president Roy Andersen said on Thursday.

The index would be calculated by cross referencing over time the rand value of the crime with the type of fraud involved. This would allow analysis of fraud by the authorities in much the same way stockwatchers follow movements in share indices.

Andersen was speaking at a conference of the Institute of Internal Auditors of South Africa (IIA). He said the IIA should also provide a periodic fraud briefing, because fraud and corruption in South African business had a high profile which could deter foreign investors.
The IIA has put together a task team to look at the proposals and is expected to have data ready for publication by early next year.
